hook: 84% survival rate — if it's caught early.
caption: Oral cancer has one of the starkest early-detection gaps in medicine. Caught in its earliest stage, the survival rate sits at 84%. Caught late, that number drops below 40%. The difference often comes down to whether someone noticed a symptom and acted on it. A sore that won't heal, a patch that looks off, a lump that's been there longer than two weeks — these are worth checking. It takes two minutes to run through a free risk screener at oralcheck.org.
